segmentation.text: walking or otherwise traveling on a sidewalk
who encounters an obstruction to his or her mobility on the sidewalk,
including, without limitation, a short section of the sidewalk that is missing or impassable,
to move around such an obstruction.

(a) Must walk or otherwise travel as far to the side of the highway near the sidewalk as possible; (b) May walk or otherwise travel on the highway in the direction he or she was walking or traveling on the sidewalk, regardless of the direction of traffic; (c) May walk or otherwise travel in a lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters if the area between the lane and the sidewalk is impassable;
and (d) Must return to the sidewalk

elements.justification: Pedestrian aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...').
Moving (drv.motion.moving) with the footprint on st.sidewalk 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line' (rel.occupies).

st.obstruction 'a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user' within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of the pedestrian's body (st.region_geometry) while it is on the sidewalk (rel.occupies).
Proceeding: the pedestrian moves on (drv.motion.moving) off the sidewalk; the detour episode.
The pedestrian's footprint on the st.highway the sidewalk lies on (st.on_way), and on no st.sidewalk.
Purpose read through conduct: the detour about the encountered obstruction (st.region_geometry distance to it).
The same pedestrian on its detour.
Returning to the sidewalk: the pedestrian's footprint overlaps a st.sidewalk again (rel.occupies).

operationalizations.convention: Walking-time convention: once clear of the obstruction (farther than the encounter reach from every obstruction, st.region_geometry), a pedestrian can step back onto the sidewalk within the time needed to walk a few metres at the design walking speed; staying off the sidewalk (rel.occupies of st.sidewalk false) and clear of every obstruction for longer than that time (a .time window, kin.time) is not as soon as practicable.

assumptions.meaning: A short section of the sidewalk on which the pedestrian is travelling is missing or cannot be passed on foot, at the place the pedestrian leaves it.

residues.why: 'With due care' qualifies the permission to leave the sidewalk; the duty to return applies to such a pedestrian whether or not care was taken, so the words add no restriction to this duty.

applicability: x is a pedestrian. Judged at each observation of a detour: x's footprint overlaps a highway region h (st.highway) and no sidewalk, and x has been off every sidewalk continuously since an observation at which x was moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance) on a sidewalk w lying on h (st.on_way w h), at which either an obstruction (st.obstruction) was within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of x's body (st.region_geometry) or asm.sidewalk_section_missing_or_impassable held.
obligation: It is not the case that, at every observation of the time window of length p.sidewalk_return_time behind the judged observation, x's footprint overlapped no sidewalk and x's body was farther than p.obstruction_encounter_reach from every obstruction (st.region_geometry); a window reaching before the start of the recording is unknown.

narrowings.why: The purpose of moving around the obstruction is read through the detour conduct.

'As soon as practicable' is read from the moment the pedestrian is clear of every obstruction; where the detour was triggered only by the declared missing or impassable section, being clear of it is read as being clear of every obstruction object.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x leaves sidewalk w at a st.obstruction (barrier), passes it on the roadway, and keeps walking on the roadway 20 s after it is more than 2 m from the barrier, a sidewalk beside it.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, but x steps back onto w 2 s after clearing the barrier.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x walks on the sidewalk throughout.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but st.region_geometry is absent, so neither the encounter nor clearing the obstruction can be read.

param_proposals.name: p.obstruction_encounter_reach
param_proposals.convention: Distance between a pedestrian's body and an obstruction within which the pedestrian is at the obstruction (encountering it, or moving around it).
param_proposals.source: Pedestrian lateral clearance and shy distance (AASHTO Guide for the Planning, Design and Operation of Pedestrian Facilities)

param_proposals.name: p.sidewalk_return_time
param_proposals.convention: Time within which a pedestrian who has cleared an obstruction steps back onto the sidewalk: the walking time to cover a few metres at the design walking speed.
param_proposals.source: MUTCD pedestrian walking speed 3.5 ft/s (1.07 m/s)

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of the acquisition standard (carla_scene_graph kinematics)
